Bimuelos (Hanukkah Honey Fritters)

Served at: Hanukkah (Festival of Lights)

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 20-25 min (plus cooling for syrup)

Bimuelos are light, airy fried dough fritters, often soaked in a sweet syrup, traditionally enjoyed by Sephardic Jews during Hanukkah. Their preparation involves frying in oil, symbolizing the miracle of the oil that lasted eight days in the Temple. They are a delightful, sweet treat perfect for celebrating the Festival of Lights.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) warm water
  • 1 teaspoon active dry yeast
  • 1 tablespoon granulated sugar (for dough)
  • 2 cups (240 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • Vegetable oil, for deep frying
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water (for syrup)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar (for syrup)
  • 1 cinnamon stick (optional)
  • 1 strip lemon peel (optional)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and 1 tablespoon granulated sugar. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. Add the flour and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix until a soft, sticky dough forms; do not overmix.
  3. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  4. While the dough rises, prepare the syrup: combine 1/2 cup water, honey, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel (if using) in a small saucepan.
  5. Bring the syrup mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove from heat, discard cinnamon and lemon peel, and let cool completely.
  6. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or deep fryer, heat about 3-4 inches (7-10 cm) of vegetable oil to 350°F (175°C).
  7. Dip your fingers in a little oil or water to prevent sticking. Pinch off small pieces of dough (about 1 tablespoon each) and carefully drop them into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pot.
  8. Fry the bimuelos for 2-3 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until they are golden brown and puffed.
  9. Remove the fried bimuelos with a slotted spoon and place them on a wire rack set over paper towels to drain excess oil.
  10. While still warm, dip each bimuelo into the cooled honey syrup, ensuring it's fully coated.
  11. Arrange on a platter and serve immediately.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, you can add a pinch of ground cinnamon or orange zest to the dough.
  • Ensure the oil temperature remains consistent for even cooking; use a thermometer if possible.
  • Bimuelos are best enjoyed fresh, but leftovers can be gently reheated in a warm oven.
